channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: SpaceX and Tesla — a Strange, But Certain, Merger
item.description: One rationale for merging SpaceX with Tesla is that the ever-busy Elon Musk could do just one earnings call per quarter instead of two. Hardly decisive, perhaps, but the conceit of prioritizing his preferences is salient enough. Talk of combining Space Exploration Technologies Corp. with Tesla Inc. overshadowed the quarterly calls of both companies this week. The results, however, illustrated just how odd this merger would be.
item.dc:creator: Liam Denning

item.title: Governments Must Not Test Limits of Global Economy's Resilience
item.description: Somewhat unexpectedly, the global economy has weathered the challenges of the past few years extraordinarily well. Following the pandemic, shock followed shock — Russia’s war on Ukraine, Washington’s rejection of rule-based liberal trade, then most recently the war with Iran. Any one of these might’ve led you to expect a severe economic setback, let alone all three combined. Yet global output kept on growing.
item.dc:creator: The Editors

item.title: In You Can See Everything, Nathan Fielder Feeds Our Grifter Obsession
item.description: When it comes to pop culture centered on Elizabeth Holmes, the disgraced former CEO of the health technology startup Theranos, audiences clearly want all they can get.
item.dc:creator: Miles Surrey

item.title: Supreme Court Originalism Is Blinding Justices to Real-World Harm
item.description: If there’s ever been a strategic thinker on the US Supreme Court, it’s Justice Elena Kagan. So you can be absolutely certain that there was careful thinking behind Kagan’s pointed criticism of the court’s conservative majority in a public interview Tuesday at Catholic University’s law school in Washington.
item.dc:creator: Noah Feldman

item.title: Trump Deserves the Political Blowback for Inflation
item.description: Of all the factors dragging down Republicans’ odds of success in the coming midterms, inflation seems to be the most important. According to the Real Clear Politics aggregation of polling results, 70.1% of Americans disapprove of President Donald Trump’s handling of inflation, and just 27.3% approve. Inflation also consistently ranks as one of the top two or three issues on voters’ minds.
item.dc:creator: Justin Fox

item.title: The Good Guys Notch a Victory in the AI-Cybersecurity Era
item.description: The headlines were unremarkable. Researchers had found a way to weaponize two vulnerabilities in PHP, a programming language used for websites and apps, and companies were being urged on Wednesday to install a patch. A smattering of websites and services were taken offline while it was installed. The US said it was looking into government systems and expediting mitigations. The media barely blinked.
item.dc:creator: Dave Lee

item.title: You Can See Everything Highlights the Challenge of AI Whistleblowers
item.description: There’s a scene in the new Elizabeth Holmes pseudo-documentary You Can See Everything that Theranos whistleblower Tyler Shultz says almost made him jump out of his chair and yell at the screen.
item.dc:creator: Beth Kowitt

item.title: It's AI 0, German Philosophers 1
item.description: It might sound like a Monty Python sketch updated for 2026: Artificial Intelligence vs. German philosophers. The question to be settled is what it means to be human in an age when AI becomes more intelligent than we are.
item.dc:creator: Andreas Kluth

item.title: Vivek Ramaswamy’s Cruel Campaign Ad Goes Too Far
item.description: For much of the Donald Trump era, no low has been too low for what passes as political rhetoric. Posting an AI slop video of the president dropping poop on protesters from a fighter jet? That’s “satire.” Calling Puerto Rico a “floating island of garbage”? Hilarious. Disparaging women as “incapable” and even “piggy”? That’s just telling it how it is.
item.dc:creator: Erika D. Smith

item.title: Trump’s Deportation Numbers Don’t Add Up
item.description: If all you had to go by was the Trump administration’s statements and press releases, you might think that “the largest deportation operation in American history” was closing in on its goal of deporting a million undocumented immigrants a year and that most of them were hardened criminals who represented “the worst of the worst.” Unfortunately, that is all that most Americans have had to go by: The administration has squelched its data on immigration enforcement, which used to be provided monthl
item.dc:creator: James Gibney

item.title: Midterms: Brace for a Market Mess — and Opportunity
item.description: The 2018 elections led to a brutal selloff, then a rebound through the next year
item.dc:creator: John Authers

item.title: France Protests: Why the Pink Panther Joined the French Uprisings
item.description: As horrific as the images of looting and arson in Paris over the weekend were, I was most unnerved by the video footage from Reuters of a man and woman calmly having evening drinks at an outdoor table of a cafe not far from the Arc de Triomphe. A fire burns in the near distance, dramatically reflected in the window of the establishment, where a server in white attends to at least one customer inside.
item.dc:creator: Howard Chua-Eoan

item.title: The Standard of Living Play: Keynes Was Right About More Than Economics
item.description: In the best scene in The Standard of Living, James Graham’s new play about John Maynard Keynes, Keynes and fellow economist Friedrich Hayek are on fire duty on the roof of King’s College chapel, locked in debate as they wait for German bombs to drop. It’s all the better for being based in fact.
item.dc:creator: Adrian Wooldridge

item.title: Oil Market Fragmentation Is Making Crude Both Cheap and Expensive
item.description: With oil, as with real estate, it’s all about location, location, location. The petroleum market has never been truly global, but rather a loosely connected collection of regional sources. When prices diverged, barrels were shuttled to the most lucrative destination. But with freight rates ballooning to prohibitively expensive levels, the region-to-region flow has been disrupted. The result? The the oil market is fragmenting.
item.dc:creator: Javier Blas

item.title: Indonesia Makes MSCI Problem Worse With Rate Miss
item.description: Indonesia’s new economic team flubbed its first real test. Faced with renewed weakness in markets, the central bank didn’t deliver on an interest rate increase on Wednesday, which would’ve helped contain the damage from a likely downgrade by MSCI Inc.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Moss

item.title: Lily Allen, Slayyyter, Charli XCX Cancel Shows: Is the Flu to Blame?
item.description: Performers and fans are falling ill right and left. The unusually early bout of H1N1 might be to blame.
item.dc:creator: Jessica Karl

item.title: Starlink: Musk Is Getting It Wrong on India’s Space Oligarchs
item.description: Elon Musk may have many strengths. Self-awareness is not one of them.
item.dc:creator: David Fickling

item.title: Nvidia Is AI’s Central Bank. Now Jensen Huang Must Step Up
item.description: An AI startup backed by Nvidia Corp. is like a fresh graduate with a Harvard degree. The pedigree brings prestige and a premium. But global investors are starting to question how much that fancy label is really worth.
item.dc:creator: Shuli Ren

item.title: Obviously SpaceX and Tesla Will Merge
item.description: Also withdrawal calculators and personal liquidity.
item.dc:creator: Matt Levine

item.title: SpaceX’s AI Surprise Is Fragile Without Grok Demand
item.description: Elon Musk has had a long, torrid relationship with artificial intelligence, dating back at least a decade to his ill-fated co-founding of OpenAI with Sam Altman. That’s rightfully made some SpaceX investors nervous about what he’s building with all the resources xAI has at its disposal since being folded into Musk’s space company in February.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Black
